G5400.def:
φόβητρον (LTr., WH, -θρον), -ου, τό 
(φοβέω), [in LXX: Ésaïe 19:17 (חָגָא) * ;] 
that which causes fright, a terror: pl. (as always, exc.Isa, l.with), Luc 21:11 (Hipp., Plat.).†

G5401.def:
φόβος, -ου, ὁ 
[in LXX chiefly for יִרְאָה, also for פַּחַד, אֵימָה, etc. ;] 
__1. in Hom., flight. 
__2. That which causes flight, fear, dread, terror: Luc 1:12, Actes 5:5, 1 Timothée 5:20. 1 Jean 4:18, al.; cogn. accusative, φοβεῖσθαι φ., Marc 4:41, Luc 2:9; with genitive obj., Jean 7:13 19:33 20:19, Hébreux 2:5, 1 Pierre 3:14 (but cf. ICC, in l);ἀπὸ (τοῦ) φ., Matthieu 14:26, Luc 21:26; εἰς φ., Romains 8:15; μετὰ φόβου, Matthieu 28:8; φ. καὶ τρόμος (Lft., Notes, 172), 1 Corinthiens 2:3, 2 Corinthiens 7:15, Éphésiens 6:5, Philippiens 2:12; by meton., of that which causes fear, Romains 13:3; of reverential fear, Romains 13:7, 1 Pierre 1:17 2:18 3:2 3:15; τ. κυρίου, Actes 9:31, 2 Corinthiens 5:11 (see Field, Notes, 183); Χριστοῦ, Éphésiens 5:21; θεοῦ, Romains 3:18, 2 Corinthiens 7:1 
SYN.: see: δειλία (and of. DCG, i, 381)

G5402.def:
φοίβη, -ης, ἡ 
Phæbe, a deaconess of Cenchræa: Romains 16:1.†

G5403.def:
φοινίκη, -ης, ἡ 
Phænicia: Actes 11:19 15:3 21:2 (see DB, iii, 856b, 857a.n).†

G5404.def:
Φοῖνιξ (on the accent, see Bl., § 4, 2; WM, § 6, lc), -ικος, ὁ, 
[in LXX for תָּמָר תִּמֹּר ;] 
the date palm, palm: τὰ βαΐα τῶν φ., Jean 12:13; of palm branches, φοίνικες (as Arist., 2Ma.10:7, al.), Apocalypse 7:9.†

G5405.def:
φοῖνιξ, -ικος, ο, ἡ 
Phænix, a city of Crete: Actes 27:12.†

G5406.def:
φονεύς, -έως, ὁ
(φόνος) [in LXX: Wis.12:5 * ;] 
a murderer: Matthieu 22:7 Actes 7:52 28:4, 1 Pierre 4:15, Apocalypse 21:8 22:15; ἀνὴρ φ., Actes 3:14.†
SYN.: ἀνθρωποκτόνος

G5407.def:
φονεύω
(φονεύς), [in LXX chiefly for רָצַח ;] 
to kill, murder. absol., Matthieu 5:21, Jacques 4:2; μὴ (οὐ) φονεύσῃς (-εις), Matthieu 5:21 19:18, Marc 10:19, Luc 18:20, Romains 13:9, Jacques 2:11 (all from Exode 20:13-14); with accusative, Matthieu 23:31, 35, Jacques 5:6.†

G5408.def:
φόνος, -ου, ὁ 
[in LXX for דָּם, פֶּה, etc. ;] 
murder, slaughter: Marc 15:7, Luc 23:19, 25, Actes 9:1, Romains 1:29; φ. μαχαίρης (cf. Exode 17:13, al.), Hébreux 11:37; pl., Matthieu 15:19, Marc 7:21, Apocalypse 9:21.†

G5409.def:
φορέω, -ῶ 
[in LXX: Proverbes 16:23 (יָסַף hi.), Sir.11:5, al. ;] 
frequent. of φέρω, denoting repeated or habitual action (cf. Tr., Syn., § lviii), most commonly used of clothing, weapons, etc., to bear constantly, wear: Matthieu 11:8, Jean 19:5, Romains 13:4, 1 Corinthiens 15:49, Jacques 2:3.†

G5410.def:
φόρον, -ου, τό
(Lat. forum): Ἀππίου Φ., see: Ἄππιος

G5411.def:
φόρος, .-ου, ὁ
(φέρω), [in LXX chiefly for מַס, also for מִדָּה, etc. ;] 
tribute paid by a subject nation (cf. 1Ma.10:33): φ. δοῦναι (1Ma.8:4 1Mac 8:7), Luc 20:22 23:2; ἀποδοῦναι, Romains 13:7; τελεῖν, Romains 13:6 (Hdt., al.).†
SYN.: κῆνσος, τέλος (which see)

G5412.def:
φορτίζω
(φόρτος), [in LXX: Eze.16:33 (שָׁחַד) * ;] 
to load: with dupl. accusative, Luc 11:46; pass., to be laden: metaphorically (EV, heavy laden), Matthieu 11:28.†

G5413.def:
φορτίον, -ου, τό
(dimin. of φόρτος), [in LXX chiefly for מַשָּׂא ;] 
a burden, load: of the cargo of a ship (Hdt., al.), Actes 27:10; metaphorically, Matthieu 11:30 23:4, Luc 11:46, Galates 6:5.†
SYN.: βάρος (which see), ὄγκος

G5415.def:
φορτούνατος (Rec. Φουρ-, see Mayser, 116 f.), -ου, ὁ 
(Lat.) Fortunatus: 1 Corinthiens 16:17 (see Lft., Cl. Ro., 1Co., 59).†

G5416.def:
φραγέλλιον, -ου, τό
(Lat. flagellum), a scourge: Jean 2:15.†

G5417.def:
φραγελλόω, -ῶ
(φραγέλλιον, which see), 
to scourge: with accusative, Matthieu 27:26, Marc 15:15 (eccl.).†

G5418.def:
φραγμός, -oῦ, ὁ
(φράσσω), [in LXX chiefly for גָּדֵר, גְּדֵרָה, also for גְּדֵרָה, etc. ;] 
__1. prop., a fencing in (Soph., OT, 1387). 
__2. = φράγμα, a fence: Matthieu 21:33, Marc 12:1, Luc 14:23. Metaphorical, μεσότοιχον (which see) τοῦ φ., genitive epexeg., Éphésiens 2:14 (see Ellic., in l).†

G5419.def:
φράζω 
[in LXX: Job 6:24 (בִּין hi.) Job 12:8 (יָרָה hi.), Dan LXX 2:4 (חָוָה pa.) * ;] 
to show forth, tell, declare, explain: Matthieu 13:36 (WH, RV, διασάφησον) Matthieu 15:15.†

G5420.def:
φράσσω 
[in LXX: Job 38:8 (סָכַךְ hi.), Osée 2:6(8) (שׂוּךְ), Proverbes 21:13 (אָטַם), etc. ;] 
to fence in, stop, close: στόματα λεόντων, Hébreux 11:33; στόμα, metaphorically, Romains 3:19; pass., καύχησις, 2 Corinthiens 11:10.†

G5421.def:
φρέαρ, -ατος, τό 
[in LXX chiefly for בְּאֵר ;] 
a well: Luc 14:5, Cantique des cantiques 4:11-12; φ. τῆς ἀβύσσου, Apocalypse 9:1-2.†

G5422.def:
φρεν-απατάω, -ῶ
(φρεναπάτης), 
to deceive one's mind (Lft., deceive by fancies, see Ga., l.with): with accusative of person(s), Galates 6:3.†

G5423.def:
φρεναπάτης, -ου, ὁ
(φρήν, ἀπάτη), 
a deceiver (B1., deceiver of his own mind, § 28, 5.2, where see ref. to π.): Tite 1:10 (eccl.).†

G5424.def:
φρήν genitive, φρενός, ἡ, 
[in LXX most frequently in Pr (Proverbes 6:32, al.) and chiefly for לֵב; also 3Ma.4:16 3Mac 5:47 ;] 
chiefly in Hom. and Trag., but also in Plat., al., both sing. and pl.; 
__1. in physical sense, the parts about the heart, midriff. 
__2. heart, mind, thought: pl., 1 Corinthiens 14:20 (see Edwards, Eng.-Gr. Lex., App., 1).†

G5425.def:
φρίσσω
(Att.. -ττω, and so 4Ma.14:9 4Mac 17:7) [in LXX: Job 4:15 ( pi.), etc. ;] 
__1. to be rough, bristle. 
__2. to shiver, shudder, tremble, from fear: Jacques 2:19 (see Hort, in l).†

G5426.def:
φρονέω, -ῶ
(φρήν), [in LXX: Deutéronome 32:29, Zacharie 9:2 (חָכָם), Psaumes 94:8 (שָׂכַל hi.), Ésaïe 44:18 (בִּין) Ésaïe 44:28, Esther 8:13, Wis.1:1 14:30, 1Ma.10:20, 2Ma.9:12; 2Ma.14:8 2Mac 14:26 * ;] 
__1. to have understanding (Hon., al.). 
__2. to think, to be minded in a certain way: ὡς νήπιος, 1 Corinthiens 13:11; with accusative (usually neut., adj., or pron., as frequently in cl.), ὃ δεῖ, Romains 12:3; ἃ, Actes 28:22; τοῦτο, Philippiens 3:15; τι ἑτέρως, ib.; οὐδὲν ἄλλο, Galates 5:10; τ. αὐτὸ φ. (Deiss., BS, 256), to be of the same mind, 2 Corinthiens 13:11, Philippiens 2:2 4:2; id. before εἰς (ἐν) ἀλλήλους(οις), Romains 12:16 15:5; τ. ἓν φ., Philippiens 2:2 (Lft., in l); before ὑπέρ, Philippiens 1:7. 
__3. to have in mind, be mindful of, think of (Hdt., Xen., al.; Es, 1Mac, ll. with): τὰ τ. θεοῦ, opposite to τ. τ. ἀνθρώπων, Matthieu 16:23, Marc 8:33; τὰ τ. σαρκός, opposite to τ. τ. πνεύρατος, Romains 8:5; τ. ἐπίγεια, Philippiens 3:19; τὰ ἄνω, opposite to τ. ἐπὶ τ. γῆς, Colossiens 3:2; τοῦτο φρονεῖτε (RV, have this mind in you), Philippiens 2:5; ὑψηλά, Romains 12:16; φ. ἡμέραν (to observe a day), Romains 14:6; before ὑπέρ, Philippiens 4:10 (cf. κατα-, παρα-, περι-, ὑπερ-φρσνέω).†

G5427.def:
φρόνημα, -τος, τό
(φρονέω), [in LXX: 2Ma.7:21 2Mac 13:9 * ;] 
that which is in the mind (the content of φρονεῖν, ICC, Ro., 88), the thought: Romains 8:6-7, 27.†

G5428.def:
φρόνησις, -εως, ἡ
(φρονέω), [in LXX for בִּינָה, תָּבוּן, חׇכְמָה, etc. ;] 
understanding, practical wisdom, prudence: Luc 1:17, Éphésiens 1:8.†
SYN.: see: σοφία, and cf. Lft., Notes, 317

G5429.def:
φρόνιμος, -ον
(φρονέω), [in LXX for בִּין, חָכָם etc. ;] 
practically wise, sensible, prudent: Matthieu 10:16 24:45, Luc 12:42, 1 Corinthiens 10:15; opposite to μωρός, Matthieu 7:24 25:2, 4 25:8-9, 1 Corinthiens 4:10; to ἄφρων, 2 Corinthiens 11:19; φ. παρ᾽ ἑαυτῷ (EV, wise in one's own conceit), Romains 11:25 12:16 (cf. Proverbes 3:7); compar., -ώτερος, Luc 16:8.†
SYN.: see: σοψός

G5431.def:
φροντίζω
(φροντίς, thought), [in LXX: 1 Rois 9:5 (דָּאַג), Psaumes 40:17 (חָשַׁב), al. ;] 
to give heed, take thought (in cl. usually absol., with accusative, with genitive), with inf., Tite 3:8 (see Bl., § 69, 4; M, Pr., 206 f.).†

G5432.def:
φρουρέω, -ῶ 
(φρουρός, a guard), [in LXX: I Esther 4:56, Jdth.3:6, Wis.17:16, 1Ma.11:3 * ;] 
to guard, keep under guard, protect or keep by guarding: 2 Corinthiens 11:32; metaphorically, Galates 3:23, Philippiens 4:7, 1 Pierre 1:5.†

G5433.def:
φρυάσσω
(so Ps, l.with, NT; elsewhere depon., φρυάσσομαι, Att.. -ττ-), [in LXX: Psaumes 2:1 (רָגַשׁ), 2Ma.7:34 R, 3Ma.2:2 * ;] 
prop., of horses, to neigh, whinny and prance (Plut., al.). Metaphorical, to be wanton, insolent: Actes 4:25 (LXX).†

G5434.def:
φρύγανον, -ου, τό
(φρύγω, to parch), [in LXX chiefly for קַשׁ, also for חָרוּל, etc. ;] 
a dry stick: pl., brushwood: Actes 28:3.†

G5435.def:
φρυγία, -ας, ἡ
(prop., the adj., Φρυγίος, -α, -ον; sc. γῆ, χώρα), 
Phrygia, a region of Asia Minor: Actes 2:10; Φ. καὶ Γαλατικὴ χώρα (Γ. χ. κ. Φ.), Actes 16:6 18:23 (on these phrases see DB, i, 89 f.; CGT, Gal., xxii f.).†

G5437.def:
φυγή, -ῆς, ἡ
(φεύγω), [in LXX chiefly for מָנוֹס and cogn. forms ;] 
flight: Matthieu 24:20.†

G5439.def:
φυλακίζω 
[in LXX: Wis.18:4 * ;] 
to imprison: Actes 22:19.†

G5440.def:
φυλακτήριον, -ου, τό 
__1. an outpost, fortification (Thuc., al.). 
__2. a safeguard (Plat.). 
__3. an amulet (Plut., al.); in NT for the Talmudic תְּפִלִּין, a prayer fillet, a phylactery, a small strip of parchment on which portions of the law were written and worn on the forehead and next the heart (cf. Exode 13:16): Matthieu 23:5.†

G5441.def:
φύλαξ, -ακος, ὁ
(φυλάσσω), [in LXX for שָׁמַר, צוּר ;] 
a guard, keeper: Actes 5:23 12:6, 19.†

G5443.def:
φυλή, ῆς, ἡ
[in LXX chiefly for; מַטֶּה, also for שֵׁבֶט, מִשְׁפָּחָה, etc. ;] 
a body of men united by kinship or habitation, a clan or tribe: of the tribes of Israel, Matthieu 19:28, Luc 2:36 22:30, Actes 13:21, Romains 11:1, Philippiens 3:5, Hébreux 7:13-14, Jacques 1:1, Apocalypse 5:5 7:4-8 21:12; of the tribes of the earth, the peoples and nations, Matthieu 24:30, Apocalypse 1:7 5:9 7:9 11:9 13:7 14:6.†

G5444.def:
φύλλον, -ου, τό 
[in LXX chiefly for עָלֶה ;] 
a leaf: Matthieu 21:19 24:32, Marc 11:13 13:28, Apocalypse 22:2.†

G5445.def:
φύραμα, -τος, τό
(φυράω, to mix), [in LXX: Exode 8:3 (Exode 7:28) Exode 12:34 (מִשְׁאֶרֶת), מִשְׁאֶרֶת), Nombres 15:20-21 (עֲרִיסָה) * ;] 
that which is mixed or kneaded, a lump: of dough, Romains 11:16, 1 Corinthiens 5:6-7, Galates 5:9; of clay, Romains 9:21.†

G5447.def:
φυσικῶς 
adv., 
naturally, by nature: Ju 10.†

G5448.def:
φυσιόω, -ῶ
(φῦσα, bellows), = cl. φυσάω, 
to puff or blow up, inflate. Metaphorical, to puff up, make proud: 1 Corinthiens 8:1. Pass., to be puffed up with pride: 1 Corinthiens 4:18-19 5:2 13:4; before ὑπό, Colossiens 2:18; before ὑπὲρ . . . κατά, 1 Corinthiens 4:6 (on the form of the subjc., see M, Pr., 54; Bl., § 22, 3).†

G5450.def:
φυσίωσις, -εως, ἡ
(φυσιόω), 
a puffing up, swelling with pride: pl., 2 Corinthiens 12:20.†

G5451.def:
φυτεία, -ας, ἡ
(φυτεύω), [in LXX: 4Ki.19:29 (נָטַע), Michée 1:6, Eze.17:7 (מַטָּע) * ;] 
__1. a planting (Xen., al.; LXX). 
__2. = φύτευμα, that which is planted, a plant (Inscr.): Matthieu 15:13.†

G5452.def:
φυτεύω
(φυτόν, a plant, φύω), [in LXX chiefly for נָטַע, also for שָׁתַל, etc. ;] 
to plant: Luc 17:28, 1 Corinthiens 3:6-8; with accusative, φυτείαν, Matthieu 15:13; ἀμπελῶνα, Matthieu 21:33, Marc 12:1, Luc 20:9, 1 Corinthiens 9:7; pass., before ἐν, Luc 13:6 17:6.†

G5453.def:
φύω
[in LXX: Proverbes 26:9, Eze.37:8 (עָלָה), etc. ;] 
__1. trans., to bring forth, produce (of men, to beget); pass., to spring up, grow: Luc 8:6, 8. 
__2. Intrans., in 2 aor., pf., plpf., and rarely in present (see LS, see word, A, II.), to spring up: Hébreux 12:15.†

G5454.def:
φωλεός, -οῦ ὁ 
a hole, den, lair: Matthieu 8:20, Luc 9:58.†

G5455.def:
φωνέω, -ῶ 
(φωνή), [in LXX for קָרָא (Jérémie 17:11, al.), etc. ;] 
__I. Intrans. 
__1. Of persons, to call out, cry out, speak aloud: Luc 8:8; φωνῇ μεγάλῃ, Marc 1:26, Actes 16:28; ἐφώνησε (φωνῇ μεγάλῇ) λέγων, Luc 8:54, Apocalypse 14:18; φωνήσαντες ἐπύθοντο, Actes 10:18. 
__2. Of the cries of animals (rarely in cl.; Ésaïe 38:14, Je, l.with): of a cock, to crow, Matthieu 26:34, Marc 14:30, Luc 22:3, Jean 13:38 18:27. 
__II. Trans. (in cl. chiefly poët.), with accusative of person(s), to call, summon, invite: Matthieu 20:32 27:47, Marc 9:35 10:49 15:35, Luc 14:12 16:2 19:15, Jean 1:49 2:9 4:16 10:3 11:28 12:17 18:33, Actes 9:41 10:7; to address, call by name (Soph.), Jean 13:13 (cf. ἀνα-, ἐπι-, προσ-, συν-φωνέω).†

G5458.def:
φωστήρ, -ῆρος, ὁ
(φῶς), [in LXX: Genèse 1:14, 16 (מָאוֹר), Dan LXX 12:3 (זֹהַר), I Esther 8:79, Wis.13:2, Sir.43:7 * ;] 
a luminary, light: Philippiens 2:15, Apocalypse 21:11.†
SYN.: φέγγος, φῶς

G5459.def:
φωσ-φόρος, -ον
(φῶς, φέρω), 
light-bringing; as subst., ὁ φ., the morning star (Plat., al.; cf. ἐωσφόρος, Ésaïe 14:12, Job 3:9, Psaumes 110:3): metaphorically, 2 Pierre 1:19 (see Mayor, in l).†

G5460.def:
φωτεινός (WH, φωτινός), ή, όν
(φῶς), [in LXX: Sir.17:31 23:19 * ;] 
bright, light: νεφέλη, Matthieu 17:5; opposite to σκοτεινός, Matthieu 6:22, Luc 11:34, 36.†

G5461.def:
φωτίζω
(φῶς) [in LXX for אוֹר hi, יָרָה hi., etc. ;] 
__1. intrans., to shine, give light (Arist., Plut., a1.): before ἐπί, Apocalypse 22:5. 
__2. Trans. 
__(a) to illumine, enlighten (Diod., Plut., al.): with accusative, Luc 11:36, Apocalypse 21:23; pass., Apocalypse 18:1. Metaphorical, of spiritual enlightenment (Psaumes 119:130, Sir.45:17, al.): Jean 1:9, Éphésiens 1:18 3:9, R, txt., Hébreux 6:4 10:32; 
__(b) to bring to light, make known (Polyb.): 1 Corinthiens 4:5, Éphésiens 3:9, R, mg., 2 Timothée 1:10 (cf. Kennedy, Sources, 107 f.).†

G5462.def:
φωτισμός, -οῦ, ὁ
(φωτίζω) [in LXX: Job 3:9, Psaumes 27:1 44:3 78:14 139:11 (אוֹר), Psaumes 89:8 (מָאוֹר) * ;] 
illumination, light: metaphorically, 1 Corinthiens 4:4 4:6.†

G5463.def:
χαίρω 
[in LXX for שָׂמַח (Genèse 45:16, al.), גִּיל (Proverbes 2:14, al.), etc.; inf., as greeting (see infr.), Ésaïe 48:22 57:21 שָׁלוֹם), 1Ma.10:18, 2Ma.1:1 and frequently in these books ;] 
__1. to rejoice, be glad: Marc 14:11, Luc 15:5, 32 19:6, 37 22:5 23:8, Jean 8:56 20:20, Actes 5:41 8:39 11:23 13:48, 2 Corinthiens 6:10 7:7 13:9, Philippiens 2:17, 28, Colossiens 2:5, 1 Thessaloniciens 5:16, 1 Pierre 4:13, 3Jn.3; χ. καὶ ἀγαλλιᾶσθαι, Matthieu 5:12; κ. σκιρτᾶν, Luc 6:23; opposite to κλαίειν, Romains 12:15, 1 Corinthiens 7:30; to κλαίειν κ. θρηνεῖν Jean 16:20; to λύπην ἔχειν, Jean 16:22; with cogn. accusative, χ. χαρὰν μεγάλην, Matthieu 2:10; χαρᾷ χ. (B1., § 38, 3; Dalman, Words, 34 f.), Jean 3:29; ἡ χαρὰ ᾗ χαίρομεν, 1 Thessaloniciens 3:9; with prep. (Bl., 38, 2), ἐπί, with dative (simple dative in cl.), Matthieu 18:13, Luc 1:14 13:17, Actes 15:31, Romains 16:19, 1 Corinthiens 13:6 16:17, 2 Corinthiens 7:13, Apocalypse 11:10; διά, Jean 3:29 11:15, 1 Thessaloniciens 3:9; ἐν, Philippiens 1:18; ἀπό, 2 Corinthiens 2:3; with accusative (Dem.), Philippiens 2:18; before ὅτι, Jean 14:28, 2 Corinthiens 7:9 7:16, 2Jn.4; ἐν τούτῳ ὅτι, Luc 10:20; with dative, Romains 12:1; ἐν κυρίῳ, Philippiens 4:10 
__2. In salutations, imperat., χαῖρε, χαίρετε, 
__(a) at meeting, hail: Matthieu 26:49 27:29, Marc 15:18, Luc 1:28, Jean 19:3; pl., Matthieu 28:9; so χχαίρειν λέγω, to give greeting, II Jn 11; in letters, χαίρειν (sc. λέγει; 81, 1), greeting: Actes 15:23 23:26 Jacques 1:1; 
__(b) at parting, farewell: 2 Corinthiens 13:11; 
__(with) on other occasions, be of good cheer: ἐν κυρίῳ, Philippiens 3:1 4:4 (cf. συν-χαίρω).†

G5464.def:
χάλαζα, -ης, ἡ
[in LXX chiefly for בָּרָד ;] 
hail: Apocalypse 8:7 11:19 16:21.†

G5466.def:
Χαλδαῖος, -ου, ὁ 
a Chaldæan: γῆ Χαλδαίων, Actes 7:4.†

G5468.def:
χαλιναγωγέω, -ῶ
(χαλινός, ἄγω), 
to lead with a bridle; metaphorically, to bridle, restrain: with accusative, γλῶσσαν, Jacques 1:26; σῶμα, Jacques 3:2.†

G5469.def:
χαλινός, -οῦ, ὁ 
[in LXX chiefly for מֶתֶג ;] 
a bridle: Jacques 3:3, Apocalypse 14:20.†

G5470.def:
χάλκεος, -έα, -εον (-οῦς, -ῆ, -οῦν) 
(χαλκός), [in LXX chiefly for נְחֹשֶׁת ;] 
brazen (i.e. of copper): Apocalypse 9:20.†

G5471.def:
χαλκεύς, -έως, ὁ
(χαλκός), [in LXX for חָרָשׁ, etc. ;] 
a worker, in metal, esp. a copper-smith: 2 Timothée 4:14.†

G5472.def:
χαλκηδών, -όνος, ὁ 
chalcedony, "supposed to denote a green silicate of copper found in the mines near Chalcedon " (Swete): Apocalypse 21:19.†

G5473.def:
χαλκίον, -ου, τό
(χαλκός), [in LXX: Job 41:22(23) (סִיר), etc. ;] 
a brazen (copper) vessel: Marc 7:4.†

G5474.def:
χαλκο-λίβανον, -ου, τό 
chalcolibanus, probably "a mixed metal of great brilliance" (Swete): Apocalypse 1:15 2:18 (RV, burnished brass).†

G5475.def:
χαλκός, -oῦ, ὁ 
[in LXX chiefly for נְחֹשֶׁת ;] 
copper: 1 Corinthiens 13:1, Apocalypse 18:12; by meton., of copper coin, Matthieu 10:9, Marc 6:8 12:41.†

G5476.def:
χαμαί 
adv., 
on or to the ground: Jean 9:6 18:6.†

G5477.def:
Χαναάν, ἡ indecl. (Heb. כְּנַעַן), 
Canaan: Actes 7:11; γῆ Χ., Actes 13:19.†

G5479.def:
χαρά, -ᾶς, ἡ
(χαίρω), [in LXX for שִׂמְחָה, שָׂשׂוֹן, etc. ;] 
joy, delight: Luc 1:14 15:7, 10, Jean 15:11 16:22, 24 17:13, Actes 8:8, 2 Corinthiens 1:24 7:13 8:2, Galates 5:22, Colossiens 1:11, Philippiens 2:2, 1 Jean 1:4, 2Jn.12; opposite to κατήφεια, Jacques 4:9; to λύπη, Jean 16:20; χ. τῆς πίστεως, Philippiens 1:25; ἀγαλλιᾶσθαι (χαίρειν, which see), χαρᾷ, Jean 3:29, 1 Pierre 1:8; χ. ἔχειν, Phm 7; πληροῦν (-οῦσθαι) χαρᾶς, Actes 13:52, Romains 15:13, 2 Timothée 1:4; ποιεῖν χ. μεγάλην, Actes 15:3; ἀπὸ τῆς χ., Matthieu 13:44, Luc 24:41, Actes 12:14; ἐν χ., Romains 15:32; μετὰ χαρᾶς, Matthieu 13:20 28:8, Marc 4:16, Luc 8:13 10:17 24:52, Philippiens 1:4 2:29, Hébreux 10:34 13:17; id. beforeπνεύματος ἁγίου, 1 Thessaloniciens 1:6; χ. ἐν π. ἁ, Romains 14:17; χ. ἐπί, 2 Corinthiens 7:4; διά, 1 Thessaloniciens 3:9; ὅτι, Jean 16:21; ἵνα, III Jn 4 By meton., of the cause or occasion of joy: Luc 2:10, 2 Corinthiens 1:15, WH, txt., R, mg., Philippiens 4:1, 1 Thessaloniciens 2:19-20, Hébreux 12:2, Jacques 1:2; ἡ χ. τ. κυρίου, Matthieu 25:21, 23.†

G5480.def:
χάραγμα, -τος, τό
(χαράσσω, to engrave), 
__(a) a stamp, impress, mark: Apocalypse 13:16-17 14:9, 11 16:2 19:20 20:4 (see Deiss., BS, 240 ff.); 
__(b) a thing graven: Actes 17:29.†

G5481.def:
χαρακτήρ, -ῆρος, ὁ
(χαράσσω, to engrave), [in LXX: Lévitique 13:28 (צָרֶבֶת), 2Ma.4:10, 4Ma.15:4 א R * ;] 
__1. a tool for graving. 
__2. a stamp or impress: as on a coin or seal; metaphorically, χ. τ. ὑποστάσεως, Hébreux 1:3.†

G5482.def:
χάραξ, -ακος, ὁ
(χαράσσω), [in LXX for סֹלְלָה, מָצוֹר, etc. ;] 
__1. a pointed stake 
__2. a palisade or rampart: Luc 19:43.†

G5483.def:
χαρίζομαι
(χάρις), [in LXX: Esther 8:7 (נָתַן), Cantique des cantiques 1:4 א, Sir.12:3, 2 -4Ma.9:1-32 * ;] 
__1. to show favour or kindness: with dative of person(s), Galates 3:18. 
__2. to give freely, bestow: with accusative and dative, Luc 7:21, Actes 3:14 25:11, 16 27:24, Romains 8:32, 1 Corinthiens 2:12, Philippiens 1:29 2:9, Phm 22. 
__3. In late Gk. (= Lat. condonare), to grant forgiveness, forgive freely: of debt, Luc 7:42-43 (EGT, in l); of sin, 2 Corinthiens 2:7 2:10 12:13, Éphésiens 4:32, Colossiens 2:13 3:13 (cf. DB, ii, 57a).†

G5484.def:
therefore, because of this, for this reason 
the acc. sg form of the noun χάριν which can be used as an improper preposition, on account of, because of, for this reason Lk. 7:47; Eph. 3:1, 14; 1Jn. 3:12; for the sake of, in order to, Gal. 3:19; Tit. 1:5, 11; Jude 16; on the score of, 1Tim. 5:14*

G5485.def:
χάρις, -ιτος, ἡ Abbott-Smith does not include the article here., accusative, χάριν (χάριτα in Actes 24:27, Ju 4; see WH, App., 157), 
[in LXX chiefly for חֵן ;] 
__1. objectively, that which causes favourable regard, gracefulness, grace, loveliness of form, graciousness of speech (cl.; Ecclésiaste 10:12, Sir.21:16, al.): Colossiens 4:6; λόγοι τ. χάριτος (genitive qual.), Luc 4:22. 
__2. Subjectively, 
__(a) on the part of the giver, grace, graciousness, kindness, goodwill, favour: Luc 2:52, Actes 7:10, al.; esp. in NT of the divine favour, grace, with emphasis on its freeness and universality: Luc 1:30, Actes 14:26, Romains 1:7, 1 Corinthiens 1:3, al.; opposite to ὀφείλημα, Romains 4:4, 16; to ἔργα, Romains 11:6; 
__(b) on the part of the receiver, a sense of favour received, thanks, gratitude: Romains 6:17 7:25, al.; χ. ἔχειν, to be thankful, Luc 17:9, 1 Timothée 1:12, al. 
__3. Objectively, of the effect of grace, 
__(a) a state of grace: Romains 5:2, 2 Timothée 2:1, 1 Pierre 5:12, 2 Pierre 3:18; 
__(b) a proof or gift of grace (cl., a favour): Jean 1:16, Actes 6:8, Romains 1:5, 1 Corinthiens 3:10, 2 Corinthiens 9:8, Galates 2:9, Éphésiens 3:2, 1 Pierre 5:5, 10 al. (For fuller treatment of the NT usage, see AR, Eph., 221ff.; DB, ii, 254ff.; DCG, i, 686ff.; Cremer, see word).

G5486.def:
χάρισμα, -τος, τό
(χαρίζομαι) [in LXX: Sir.7:33 א (AB, χάρις) Sir.38:30 Bl (א AB2R, χρῖσμα) * ;] 
a gift of grace, a free gift, esp. of extra­ordinary operations of the Spirit in the Apostolic Church, but including all spiritual graces and endowments (Lft., Notes, 148 f.): Romains 1:11 5:15-16 6:23 11:29 12:6, 1 Corinthiens 1:7 7:7 12:4 12:9 12:28 12:30-31, 2 Corinthiens 1:11, 1 Timothée 4:14, 2 Timothée 1:6, 1 Pierre 4:10.†

G5487.def:
χαριτόω, -ῶ
(χάρις), [in LXX: Sir.18:17 (ἀνδρί κεχαριτωμένῳ; Vg., justificato; Syr., saintly) * ;] 
to endow with χάρις (which see), i.e. 
__1. (a) to make graceful; 
__(b) to make gracious (Sir, l.with). 
__2. In Hellenistic writings (for exx., see AR, Eph., 227; Lft., Notes, 315), 
__(a) to cause to find favour; 
__(b) to endue with grace (i.e. divine favour): Luc 1:28, Éphésiens 1:6.†

G5488.def:
χαρράν 
indecl. (in FlJ., Ant., i, 16, 1, Κάρρα, -ας, ib. 6, 5, Χαρρά, -ᾶς; so LXX: Genèse 29:4 E, Eze.27:28 B, elsewhere -άν­Heb. חָרָן), Haran, a town in N.W. Mesopotamia: Actes 7:2, 4.†

G5489.def:
χάρτης, -ου, ὁ 
[in LXX: Ésaïe 8:1 A, Jérémie 36:2, 6 36:23 (מְגִלָּה) * ;] 
a sheet of paper, made of papyrus strips (see Kennedy, Sources, 42; Milligan, NTD, 10-12; DB, iv, 945 f.): II Jn 12 (Plat., Inscr.).†

G5490.def:
χάσμα, -τος, τό
(χάσκω, to yawn), [in LXX: 2 Rois 18:17 (פַּחַת)* ;] 
a chasm, wide space: Luc 16:26.†

G5491.def:
χεῖλος, -ους, τό, genitive pl., -εων (see Bl., § 8, 4; Thackeray, Gr., I, 151), 
[in LXX chiefly for שָׂפָה ;] 
a lip (as in Heb., of the lip as the organ of speech): Matthieu 15:8, Marc 7:6, Romains 3:13, 1 Corinthiens 14:21, Hébreux 13:15, 1 Pierre 3:10" (LXX) . Metaphorical, of things, an edge, brink, etc. (Hom., Hdt., al.): of the sea­shore, Hébreux 11:12.†

G5492.def:
χειμάζω
(χεῖμα, winter cold) [in LXX: Proverbes 26:10 (†) * ;] 
__1. to expose to winter cold, go into winter quarters. 
__2. to drive with storm; pass., to be driven with storm, tempest-tossed: Actes 27:18.†

G5493.def:
χείμμαρος (shortened form of the more usual -οος, Attic contr., -ους), -ον 
(χεῖμα, ῥέω) [in LXX chiefly for נַחַל ;] 
winter-flowing; as subst., ὁ χ. (sc. ποταμός), a torrent: Jean 18:1.†

G5494.def:
χειμών, -ῶνος, ὁ 
[in LXX for גֶּשֶׁם, סְתָו ;] 
__1. winter: Jean 10:22, 2 Timothée 4:21; genitive, χειμῶνος, in winter, Matthieu 24:20, Marc 13:18. 
__2. Prop., a winter storm, hence, generally, a storm, tempest: Matthieu 16:3 (T, WH, R, mg., om.), Actes 27:20.†

G5495.def:
χείρ, genitive, χειρος (accusative, χεῖραν, 1 Pierre 5:6 T), ἡ, 
[in LXX chiefly for יָד ;] 
the hand: Matthieu 3:12, Marc 3:1, Luc 6:6, al. mult.; ἡ χ., acting subject, Luc 22:21; pl., Actes 17:25 20:34, 1 Jean 1:1; τ. ἔργα τῶν χ., Actes 7:41, Apocalypse 9:20; ὁ ἀσπασμὸς τ. ἐμῇ χ., 1 Corinthiens 16:21, Colossiens 4:18, 2 Thessaloniciens 3:17; prepositional phrases, esp. those without art., similar to Heb. constructions (Bl., §32, 4; 40, 9; 46, 9), ἐν χ.; with genitive (Lft., in l.), Galates 3:19; σὺν χ. ἀγγέλου, Actes 7:35; διὰ (τῶν) χειρῶν (διὰ χειρός), Marc 6:2, Actes 5:12 7:25, al.; ἐπὶ χειρῶν, Matthieu 4:6, Luc 4:11; ellipse of χ. (ἡ δεξία, ἀριστερα; Bl., §44, 1), Matthieu 6:3, al. By meton., for the power or activity of an individual, Matthieu 17:22, Marc 9:31, Luc 9:31, Jean 10:39, Actes 12:11, al.; metaphorically, of the activity or power of God: Luc 1:66 23:46, Jean 10:29, Actes 11:21 13:11, al.

G5496.def:
χειραγωγέω, -ῶ
(χειραγωγός), [in LXX: Juges 16:26 A (יָד חָזַק), Tob.11:16 א * ;] 
to lead by the hand: Actes 9:8 22:11.†

G5497.def:
χειρ-αγωγός, -όν
(χείρ, ἄγω) 
leading by the hand. As subst., ὁ χ., one to lead by the head, a guide: Actes 13:11.†

G5498.def:
χειρόγραφος, -ον
(χείρ, γράφω), [in LXX: Tob.5:3 9:2, 5 * ;] 
written with the hand. As subst., τὸ χ., a handwriting (Inscr., Polyb., al.): metaphorically, Colossiens 2:14.†

G5499.def:
χειρο-ποίητος, -ον
(χείρ, ποιέω), [in LXX (of idols) for אֱלִיל ;] 
made by hand (i.e. of human handiwork): of temples, Marc 14:58, Actes 7:48 17:24, Hébreux 9:11, 24; of circumcision, Éphésiens 2:11.†
